A bare frame of three words or fewer, the sentence-final noun alone, every disguised spelling and every other locale stay blocked. The clearance also fails when the text holds a hostile predicate (nojentos, lixo, odeio, morram and the like), so an insult sentence built on the noun keeps screening. Round 8d: unaccented pas (French negation) is back on the French veto list (Portuguese pás is rare); ou and tres stay out. A letter Portuguese never writes (è ù û î ë ï ü œ ÿ) anywhere in the raw text also refuses the clearance for the two rug targets. Round 8e: ü and ë left the forbidden letters (old Portuguese spellings such as lingüiça and tranqüilo, and names such as Müller and Zoë, are Portuguese or ordinary names); è ù û î ï œ ÿ stay.
